conventions.convention: Surface equivalence fixes every black boundary parameterization and preserves incoming/outgoing faces and free-boundary colors. Incoming induced orientations oppose object orientations; outgoing orientations agree.
The closed category permits no free boundary, including windows; it is not the full circle-object subcategory of the open-closed category.
TQFTs are strong symmetric monoidal functors to finite-dimensional vector spaces; their morphisms are monoidal natural transformations.

All algebraic data are over an arbitrary field. Symmetry means symmetry of the functional pairing; commutativity means invariance of multiplication under the flip. Only the closed object is required to be commutative.

Open sectors are indexed spaces A_ab, paired with A_ba. Cardy has source A_bb and target A_aa, with coproduct factors A_ba and A_ab reversed by the flip. No equality between C and a center is imposed.

Countable choice is assumed for the smooth collar and transversality construction. The empty perturbation-region case avoids parameter selection; density is invoked only for a positive-dimensional parameter ball.

Normal words retain marked interval cycles and their complete endpoint-color sequences, every colored-window multiplicity, and slot-restoring permutations. Zero-arity multiplication is the unit and zero-arity comultiplication is the counit.

load_bearing.statement: For compact oriented S-colored surfaces with the same marked source and target, equality of morphisms is equivalent to equality of the stated component partition, genera, colored-window multiplicities, cyclic marked open-boundary cycles with endpoint colors, and the multiset of genus/window data for components without marked slots. Each connected component equals its candidate normal word; disconnected words tensor with marked slot permutations restored.

Assuming ACω, every compact oriented surface with the specified black/free boundary and compatible corner collars admits the stated boundary-relative excellent Morse function and a finite decomposition into identity cylinders and the ten typed sewing generators, retaining every local color.

The typed knowledgeable equations imply the evaluation/coevaluation snakes, pairing and copairing symmetries, zipper/cozipper transports, cozipper coalgebra and counit preservation, window and handle slides, Cardy reduction, and cyclic cozipper rotation. The map identities also hold in the formal symmetric monoidal presentation; dual-isomorphism assertions are confined to the finite-dimensional vector-space specialization.

The ten generator surfaces obey the boundary-relative equalities whose images under a strong symmetric monoidal functor are precisely equations 1–7 of the knowledgeable-data definition. Each equality preserves every black parametrization, corner endpoint color, and free-boundary label; completeness is not asserted here.

For any finite-dimensional unital associative algebra over any field and any Frobenius functional ε, there is a unique basis-independent tensor e with both stated contraction identities, satisfying (a⊗1)e=e(1⊗a). The map Δ(a)=(a⊗1)e is coassociative, counital with counit ε, and satisfies both Frobenius identities. Conversely every finite-dimensional Frobenius object has nondegenerate functional pairing and this unique coproduct; symmetry is not assumed.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 treats shortening collars and increasing reparameterizations, then concludes that gluing is independent of representatives. The Definition forgets the chosen collars entirely, so it also permits two arbitrary compatible collar embeddings, which need not differ merely by normal-coordinate reparameterization. The short boundary-relative collar-comparison argument extending the seam coordinate change and preserving corner products is unstated.
The Statement says, “This formal assertion is proved by faithful bending in step 1.5”; there is no step 1.5. The faithful-bending argument is step 4.1.

In Proof tables, the delimiter and first data row occupy one source line: “|---|---|---| | 1 |”. This is not a valid standalone Markdown table delimiter and merges the first mixed-saddle factorization into it. Steps 6.1 and 7.1 rely on the six-row table.
